questions.stem: A gardener dips the cut end of a stem cutting into rooting powder before planting it in soil. The rooting powder contains synthetic auxin. Why does this help the cutting grow into a new plant?

options.text: Auxin kills bacteria on the cut surface, preventing infection
Auxin stimulates the growth of adventitious roots from the cut end of the stem
Auxin causes the cutting to photosynthesise faster
Auxin prevents the cutting from losing water through transpiration

questions.explanation: Synthetic auxin in rooting powder stimulates the rapid development of new roots (adventitious roots) from the cut stem. This allows the cutting to absorb water and minerals from the soil, establishing itself as a new, independent plant — a form of artificial vegetative propagation.

questions.stem: Selective weedkillers used on lawns kill broadleaf weeds but not grass. These weedkillers are synthetic auxins. Why do they kill weeds but not grass?

options.text: Grass does not respond to auxin at all
Broadleaf plants absorb more of the synthetic auxin, which causes uncontrolled growth and death, while narrow-leaved grasses absorb less and are unaffected
The weedkiller is applied only to the weeds, not to the grass
Grass is immune to all plant hormones

questions.explanation: Broadleaf weeds absorb more synthetic auxin due to their larger leaf surface area. The excess auxin causes uncontrolled, unsustainable growth that kills the plant. Narrow-leaved grasses absorb much less auxin and are not significantly affected, allowing selective weed removal.

questions.stem: A fruit grower wants seedless grapes. They spray the grape flowers with gibberellin solution before pollination. How does gibberellin produce seedless fruit?

options.text: Gibberellin kills the seeds after they form
Gibberellin stimulates fruit development without the need for fertilisation, so no seeds form
Gibberellin causes the flowers to fall off, and fruit grows from the stem instead
Gibberellin makes the seeds dissolve inside the fruit

questions.explanation: Gibberellins can stimulate fruit development (parthenocarpy) without fertilisation occurring. Since no fertilisation takes place, no seeds develop. The fruit still grows and ripens normally, but is seedless — a commercially valuable trait for grapes and some other fruits.

questions.stem: A banana exporter ships green bananas overseas and then exposes them to ethylene gas upon arrival. Why are bananas transported while still green?

options.text: Green bananas are lighter and cheaper to transport
Green bananas are unripe and firm, so they resist bruising during transport; ethylene can then trigger ripening at the destination
Ripe bananas cannot survive in cold storage
Green bananas taste better than yellow ones

questions.explanation: Unripe (green) bananas are firm and less prone to damage during long-distance transport. By controlling the timing of ethylene exposure, producers can trigger ripening after transport, ensuring the bananas reach consumers at the ideal stage of ripeness.

questions.stem: A plant biologist is developing dwarf varieties of wheat that are resistant to wind damage. Which plant hormone could be manipulated to achieve shorter stem growth?

options.text: Increasing gibberellin levels to promote stem elongation
Reducing gibberellin sensitivity or production to inhibit stem elongation, producing shorter plants
Increasing auxin to make the plant grow taller
Adding ethylene to promote rapid upward growth

questions.explanation: Gibberellins promote stem elongation. By breeding or engineering plants with reduced gibberellin production or sensitivity, shorter (dwarf) varieties can be produced. These are more resistant to wind damage (lodging) and can support heavier grain heads — this was key to the Green Revolution in agriculture.
